// Run starts dispatching alerts incoming via the updates channel.
func (d *Dispatcher) Run(dispatchStartTime time.Time) {
	d.done = make(chan struct{})

	d.mtx.Lock()
	d.logger.Debug("preparing to start", "startTime", dispatchStartTime)
	d.startTimer = time.NewTimer(time.Until(dispatchStartTime))
	d.state = DispatcherStateWaitingToStart
	d.logger.Debug("setting state", "state", "waiting_to_start")
	d.aggrGroupsPerRoute = map[*Route]map[model.Fingerprint]*aggrGroup{}
	d.aggrGroupsNum = 0
	d.metrics.aggrGroups.Set(0)
	d.ctx, d.cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	d.mtx.Unlock()

	d.run(d.alerts.Subscribe("dispatcher"))
	close(d.done)
}

changeset.goal: Restore A1/A2 so active alert groups stay visible through the groups API during and after a valid configuration reload; the only supported causal path (stop + rebuild dispatch.Dispatcher inside the main.go reload callback) requires an undisclosed readiness/handoff contract, so this round returns NEEDS_EVIDENCE with no executable edits and explicit open obligations.

open_obligations.statement: After a valid Alertmanager configuration reload returns, the production groups API still reports the active injected alert groups instead of an emptied aggregation map.
open_obligations.reason: V1/V2 are SUPPORTED: the reload callback stops the running dispatcher, constructs a replacement, and launches go disp.Run, whose Run resets aggrGroupsPerRoute to an empty map before re-consuming alerts; no supplied source exposes a readiness/backlog signal needed to plan a safe handoff, so the obligation stays open this round.
open_obligations.coverage_rationale: groups.visible_at_reload_return (FAIL, 19/20 reloads missing all 2048 names) directly observes the immediately-after-return state named by the statement; groups.visible_after_reload (PASS) observes a later instant. Failure of at_reload_return disproves the statement, but success of both would not exhaust all reload instants or distributed convergence, so the checks are necessary, not sufficient.

open_obligations.statement: During twenty valid configuration reloads active alert groups do not temporarily disappear from the production groups API at any sampled instant.
open_obligations.reason: The same supported path (disp.Stop then new Dispatcher whose Run empties aggrGroupsPerRoute) leaves Groups observing an empty aggregate map during the window; the missing readiness/handoff contract prevents planning a non-empty-window replacement, so the obligation remains open.
open_obligations.coverage_rationale: groups.visible_during_reload (FAIL) samples the target every 2ms across twenty reloads and observed 54/248 missing samples; it is necessary evidence that a disappearance occurs, but sampled continuity is not a proof over unsampled instants, so it is necessary rather than all-covering.

precondition_review.condition: inhibit.Inhibitor.Run creates a fresh cancelable context, starts per-rule scache goroutines and runs the inhibitor loop; the main.go reload callback calls inhibitor.Stop() and then re-runs the newly built inhibitor.
precondition_review.rationale: The inhibitor governs alert muting/inhibition consumed by notification dispatch, not the aggregation groups returned to the groups API via api.Options.GroupFunc (main.go groupFn -> disp.Groups). Neither A1 nor A2 depends on inhibitor readiness or state, so it is not a precondition of restoring groups-API visibility.

precondition_review.condition: dispatch.Dispatcher.Run resets d.aggrGroupsPerRoute to an empty map, sets state WaitingToStart and only repopulates aggregation groups by consuming d.alerts.Subscribe("dispatcher") inside run(), so the replacement dispatcher's groups state is empty until the initial alert backlog has been re-consumed.
precondition_review.rationale: No supplied source exposes a readiness or backlog-completion signal on Dispatcher.Run, so starting Run asynchronously cannot be treated as establishing a populated groups map; the handoff condition the candidate repair depends on is unresolved and must be evidenced before any executable change.

evidence_gaps.summary: No supplied source provides a readiness/completion signal for the new dispatcher, so an atomic handoff (keep the old dispatcher serving Groups until the replacement has reconstructed aggrGroupsPerRoute) cannot be planned without guessing a lifecycle contract.

provider.Alerts.Subscribe iterator semantics (whether/when the initial active-alert backlog is fully delivered after subscription) are not in the supplied evidence, so 'the new dispatcher is ready' cannot be defined or observed.

aggrGroupsPerRoute is keyed by *Route; no supplied source shows whether aggregation groups remain valid or transferable when the routing tree is rebuilt on reload, so in-place dispatcher reuse cannot be justified as safe.

// Run starts dispatching alerts incoming via the updates channel.
func (d *Dispatcher) Run(dispatchStartTime time.Time) {
	d.done = make(chan struct{})

	d.mtx.Lock()
	d.logger.Debug("preparing to start", "startTime", dispatchStartTime)
	d.startTimer = time.NewTimer(time.Until(dispatchStartTime))
	d.state = DispatcherStateWaitingToStart
	d.logger.Debug("setting state", "state", "waiting_to_start")
	d.aggrGroupsPerRoute = map[*Route]map[model.Fingerprint]*aggrGroup{}
	d.aggrGroupsNum = 0
	d.metrics.aggrGroups.Set(0)
	d.ctx, d.cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	d.mtx.Unlock()

	d.run(d.alerts.Subscribe("dispatcher"))
	close(d.done)
}
